This causes a problem because it has to combine all of those to get the amount you are sending then still have enough to be attached to All the NFT’s you have in your wallet already and be able to return the left over. In very specific circumstances it can cause a problem. They are advocating a “be safe” strategy to avoid the potential of an error. Personally, I think that the floor price is negatively influenced by a few things, e.g. wider bear market, several people in here clearly in for the 'gamble' of a legendary or mythic in hope of flipping to make rich quick. 

A lower mint price would be welcomed, as even the 'illusion' of demand by having secondary markets at a small multiple will instill confidence. 

My concerns are about 2 things though:
(1) This is ramping up valuation before launch, which is the opposite of organic growth. There's an increasing risk of asset prices dropping if the numbers of users/gamers don't match expectation in the opening weeks.
(2) There's a large volume of NFT mints planned over the next year. If mint prices are consistently high, I begin to wonder who the audience is, as it sure won't be the average gamer / citizen with just a few hundred bucks in the bank.... If average people get priced out, how do we draw the masses?

IDEA for people who keep missing
- fractional tier points for each "unsuccessful" transaction that give you a better edge on the next round
- I think it would be spam/scam resistant because you can only put one order in per mint regardless
- concept could be something we all have consensus on, like having a set fraction of a second shaved off you mint time for each "unsuccessful" attempt (points could be basis points up to either 2 or 6 decimals)
- you get more points for being closer to the cutoff

 Example: "received unsuccessful" email with time of 8.539079 seconds (round up to 8.54 or use 6 decimal)
1. Cutoff for a successful mint was 7.54 seconds
2. Difference was 1 second, time reward should be higher for the closer you are, not farther (that would get spammed)
3. Take 7.54 and divide it by 8.54 = 0.88
4. 0.88 points of time/seconds are added to the next round you participate in
5. This continues until you secure a plot, then it resets
Now if my time would have been 12.86 seconds instead of 8.54, the equation would have issued a lower reward (7.54 divided by 12.86 = 0.57 points)
 Since this is a fractional equation, the most points you could ever get for missing a mint would be 0.99 points. I feel that is a reasonable system for users who fail every time. It would need to remain consistent to only be usable in the tier level you participated in. (tier 4 points cant be used in tier 2)

 To avoid people intentionally accumulating time points for the rarer plots that come later (i.e. Copias is harder to get than the previous ones, so we don't want to incentivize near misses along the way). We would need to have time points increase the chances of getting a "common" rarity. The highest chance for rarity would still require using 0 time points.

Time points could expire for each type of asset launch, i.e. land sale points only work for further land sale points, vehicle for vehicle etc. You would be allowed the option to not use the time points. other ideas? (edited)

I think we all know that the issue is more about the supply than anything else. Everyone think it's a bot because someone has minted faster than another person but instead they must understand that we have several factors in that mint. We can take an example: 

If my best score is 4.3245 sec, someone else can do it for 4.24584 sec because: 

1- Human physiology, someone can process faster visual data and click a bouton than others. If you are 0.02 lower by any interaction and you need to do 5 interactions that will give you 1 whole second of vantage facing another minter. 
2- If you have a ping with the server you will have a delay. If the ping is between 170 and 220 ms you will again lose 1 seconds for someone with a ping between 15 and 30 ms. 
3- Wallet queue. When we press the bouton we are not only sending something to the website we are doing a queuing to the wallet. So if your PC can be slower than the PC of someone else. 
4- Browser, if you use chrome it could take longer than any other browsers to open the windows. More if you have other heavy tabs or another browser open. Temps and cookies could mess up too. Time lost or win here is in the ms area. 
5- Luck, you got unlucky with the upload of the server, the wallet opening, your machine was starting updating or processing something that make you lose time and make it impossible for you to press the bouton in less than 6 sec. (edited)

@Indy The current minting process is overall good but still needs improvement. Here are my suggestions:

TWEAKS TO TIERING:
- Add a tier for NFT2Tree holders.
- Add a tier for NFT2Tree holders who have been around for at least 30 days.
- Add a tier for vehicle NFT holders who have been around for at least 30 days.

DURING MINT EVENT:
1. On a per tier basis, once the tier period begins let people attempt to enter the queue as normal.
2. Every 20 seconds the minting system will take a snapshot of the queue.
3. When a snapshot is taken, NFT reservations will be distributed randomly to the people within that snapshot.
4. Any remaining NFT reservations will be dsitributed randomly among the next snapshot of people.
5. This continues until either the reservations sell out or the tier period ends.

PROS:
- Any bot activity that isn't caught is at least mitigated.
- People who have to suffer loading times that are out of their control have a fairer shot.
- Keeping the initial time window under a minute still rewards people who make the effort to participate on time.
- More tiers means more opportunities in general and hopefully less stress for people who qualify into multiple tiers.

CONS:
- It will be impossible to brag about selling out in under 10 seconds. (edited)

I have posted before but maybe a good read:

I think we all know that the issue is more about the supply than anything else. Everyone think it's a bot because someone has minted faster than another person but instead they must understand that we have several factors in that mint. We can take an example: 

If my best score is 4.3245 sec, someone else can do it for 4.24584 sec because: 

1- Human physiology, someone can process faster visual data and click a bouton than others. If you are 0.02 lower by any interaction and you need to do 5 interactions that will give you 1 whole second of vantage facing another minter. 
2- If you have a ping with the server you will have a delay. If the ping is between 170 and 220 ms you will again lose 1 seconds for someone with a ping between 15 and 30 ms. 
3- Wallet queue. When we press the bouton we are not only sending something to the website we are doing a queuing to the wallet. So if your PC can be slower than the PC of someone else. 
4- Browser, if you use chrome it could take longer than any other browsers to open the windows. More if you have other heavy tabs or another browser open. Temps and cookies could mess up too. Time lost or win here is in the ms area. 
5- Luck, you got unlucky with the upload of the server, the wallet opening, your machine was starting updating or processing something that make you lose time and make it impossible for you to press the bouton in less than 6 sec.

I would go for common epic over rare large. We don't have all the facts we need to make this decision in an informed way yet, so it's a lot of guesswork. We know rarer land means we get to choose its location earlier. But I am not sure if rarity will also influence the airdrops and staking rewards - nor if size will. And if both factors play a part, which one more so? But we know that in the P2E mechanism, having more land will give you more potential income for working the land or renting it out. But will this income be high enough to be important? So many unknowns. In the end, I would say epic (and obviously copias) plots will become more valuable, since they are rarer and will be more useful not only for income from working land but also for building big objects. These big objects could be good for marketing (i.e. they will be more visible). 

So, if you want to build something big, e.g. to display lots of NFTs or just get attention and potentially footfall for a business, or if you want to earn more "passive" income from working land or renting out land or accommodation, I would go for the common epic. KEY TAKEAWAYS
Capitulation happens when a significant proportion of investors succumbs to fear and sells over a short period of time, causing the price of a security or a market to drop sharply amid high trading volume.
Capitulation marks a short-term low in the price and is followed by at least a relief rally. 
Until the price rebounds significantly, there can be no assurance the apparent "capitulation" won't be followed by additional dramatic drops.
Capitulation causes heavy turnover among investors, enabling a rebound by replacing risk-averse sellers with risk-tolerant buyers, but it can't guarantee those buyers won't eventually sell even lower.

Players can earn rewards for staking specific NFTs and locking them to another NFT.
Districts
In each Themed Zone there are districts that contain land plots that can be owned by players. 
Districts are given daily rewards based on the performance of its residents. Those rewards are then split into two reward pots (see Tokenomics).
District land property owners reward pot.
District tenant rewards pot.
Land Property Owners
Land property owners receive a percentage of the district's rewards based on the number of tenants they have. To become a property owner in a district you will need to purchase a land property NFT.
For example, if the entire district has 80 residents and a single property contains 10 residents, then that individual land property owner will receive 12.5% of the district land rewards pot. As follows:
Formula = Individual Land Property Owner Rewards = Total District Residents divided by Individual Property Tenants.
Example individual land property owner rewards = (100 / 80) * 10 = 12.5% of the total district land rewards pot.
Property Levels
The property on an individual piece of land can be upgraded to increase the number of tenants in that property. This also has the effect of increasing the potential population of a district.
